_comment: he20 baseline: 'Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning' (Wang et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2506.01939v2), run on THIS project's canonical RL protocol. Every shared training parameter is copied from formal250.json so this arm is comparable with GRPO, VPO-RM, P2T and RED; only the mask differs. The paper's own contribution is a single change to an unchanged algorithm: the policy-gradient loss is computed only over the tokens whose per-token entropy is in the top entropy_top_ratio fraction of the population, and the token-count normaliser is restricted to those same tokens (its Eq. 6). The paper's baseline is DAPO; this arm's is the PROJECT's GRPO, because the project's other arms are GRPO-family and the mask is the only thing this arm is supposed to add. What that leaves out is recorded in HE20_REPRO_NOTES.md section 5: DAPO's clip-higher, dynamic sampling and token-level loss, the paper's math RLVR setting and DAPO-Math-17K, and its response cap of 20480. init_adapter must be set to the SFT checkpoint before this runs; sigma0 must be shared with the sibling arms -- this arm must not self-calibrate. entropy_top_rule: 'threshold' is the paper's Eq. (6) (every token at or above the (1-rho) quantile survives, so ties can push the kept fraction above rho); 'topk' is the authors' reference implementation (torch.topk, exactly ceil(rho*n), ties broken by index). The two differ only on ties. DEVICE PLAN: actor on 0, reward model on 1, vLLM tensor-parallel across 2 and 3. Launch with HE20_GPUS=0,1,2,3 so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES matches the trainer's device-plan check exactly rather than skipping it. push_every is 5: autopush stages the whole tree (git add -A), so unrelated working-tree files land in whichever arm pushes next.
